biography.currentRole: NC State Senator, District 8 (2011–present); Chairman, Senate Rules and Operations Committee; Chairman, Senate Finance Committee; Chairman, Select Committee on Nominations
priorRoles: Vice Chair, Brunswick Community College Board of Trustees
biography.education: B.S., North Carolina State University; Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM), University of Georgia (1976)
biography.background: Veterinarian, farmer, avid hunter and fisherman. Brunswick County native. Cancer survivor who used marijuana medicinally during chemotherapy, which motivated his medical marijuana advocacy. 14+ years as one of the most powerful legislators in NC—Rules Committee chair gives him near-total control over what bills reach the floor. District 8 covers Brunswick, Columbus, and a portion of New Hanover counties.
biography.electionHistory: Won 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, 2022, 2024. Defeated Katherine Randall (D) 60%–40% in 2024 general election. 2026 opponents: Richard Combes (D), Tim White (L).
biography.mediaEngagement: Consistent pattern of declining media interviews and candidate forums. WHQR reports he has ignored local journalist inquiries and skipped media-hosted forums for many years. Declined 2024 forum citing scheduling conflict.

campaignWebsite.notes: No dedicated campaign website identified in 2026 cycle research. Campaign committee is 'Rabon for Senate.' As of Dec 31 2025: total contributions $39,000, total expenditures $37,998.

votingRecord.notes: State legislator — no federal voting record. Long record in NC Senate 2011–present. As Rules Committee chair, he controls which bills advance; his influence is exercised procedurally as well as through floor votes.

keyVotes.bill: SB 20 — Care for Women, Children, and Families Act (2023)
keyVotes.notes: Voted to pass 12-week abortion ban. Senate passed 29-20 on party line. Also voted to override Gov. Cooper's veto (Senate 30-20, party line). ChoiceTracker labels Rabon 'Anti-Choice.' Endorsed by NC Right to Life in 2024.

keyVotes.bill: SB 20 — Care for Women, Children, and Families Act — veto override (2023)
keyVotes.notes: Confirmed party-line veto override vote; Rabon is a Republican Senate leader voting with caucus

AffordableCareNC lists Rabon as supporting the Senate version of HB76, which expanded Medicaid and reformed CON laws. Signed by governor 3/27/2023. NOTE: Senate Republicans conditioned Medicaid expansion on CON reform (market deregulation); this is NOT a straightforward endorsement of single-payer or government coverage expansion — it is a market-compatible, work-requirement-friendly version of expansion. Confidence: medium (sourced from advocacy site; individual vote record not confirmed directly).

keyVotes.bill: SB 3 — NC Compassionate Care Act / Medical Cannabis (2023)
keyVotes.notes: Rabon was lead primary sponsor of SB3, the medical marijuana bill. Senate passed 36-10 (March 2023) and 33-9 (June 2024). Bill died in House repeatedly due to House Republican opposition. Rabon publicly disclosed he used marijuana illegally during chemotherapy for cancer. NORML gave him B+ for primary sponsorship. Bill did NOT become law during 2023-2024 session.

keyVotes.bill: HB 10 — Private School Voucher Expansion / ICE Cooperation (2024)
keyVotes.vote: Yes (inferred — party-line vote, Senate Rules Chairman)
keyVotes.notes: Senate voted 30-19 along party lines to pass and then override veto. Added $463.5M to Opportunity Scholarship program; escalates to $825M/year by 2032-33. Rabon, as Senate Rules Chair and party caucus leader, would have facilitated passage of this bill. Also required sheriffs to comply with ICE detainment requests.

keyVotes.bill: SB 50 — Freedom to Carry NC (Permitless Carry) (2025)
keyVotes.notes: SB50 eliminates permit requirement to carry a concealed handgun; lowers carry age to 18. Bill passed Senate; Governor Stein vetoed June 2025; Senate voted 30-19 to override. As of Dec 2025 House veto override vote still pending. Rabon voted Yes on both passage and veto override.

Rabon is listed as co-sponsor. SB266 eliminates HB951's interim 70% carbon reduction target by 2030 (while retaining 2050 neutrality goal); allows cost-recovery for new carbon-emitting generation. Critics say it raises rates by up to $23B for ratepayers. NC Chamber of Commerce supported it. NRDC, Sierra Club, NC Justice Center opposed. Governor Stein vetoed July 2 2025; legislature overrode.

keyVotes.vote: Yes (inferred — bipartisan bill; individual vote not confirmed)
keyVotes.notes: This bipartisan clean energy bill set the 70% carbon reduction by 2030 goal and 2050 carbon neutrality target that SB266 (2025) later rolled back. The bill passed broadly with bipartisan support. Rabon's individual vote not confirmed but passage was widely supported in both chambers. His later co-sponsorship of SB266 to roll back HB951's interim targets is the stronger, more recent signal.

NC Senate passed budget with phased income tax reductions: 4.75% (2023) → 4.5% (2024) → 4.25% (2025) → 3.99% with future triggers potentially reaching 2.49%–1.99%. Rabon filed SB 651 ('Tax Relief For All') as Finance Chair to cut personal income tax below 2.5% by 2026. Budget also preserved/extended tax cuts benefiting top earners disproportionately (bottom 20% save avg $5/yr; top 1% save avg $4,000/yr per NC Budget & Tax Center).
Rabon as Finance Chair filed legislation to cut personal income tax rate below 2.5% by 2026. Strong signal of aggressive anti-tax stance.

keyVotes.bill: SB 382 — Omnibus Bill with Downzoning Ban (2024)
keyVotes.notes: SB382 enacted a sweeping ban on downzoning without all affected property owners' written consent, effectively stripping local zoning authority for density-reducing changes. Retroactive 180 days. NC Home Builders Association called it 'a huge victory for property rights.' Local governments, including towns in Rabon's district, lobbied Rabon to address concerns. Passed after Cooper veto override. Rabon's individual vote not confirmed but as Rules Chair he controlled the bill's path.

keyVotes.bill: Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (2013 committee action)
keyVotes.notes: In 2013, as Senate Finance Committee Co-chairman, Rabon declined to count a voice vote that would have ended a key renewable energy requirement, effectively blocking the repeal. This is a decade-old signal and is superseded by his 2025 co-sponsorship of SB266 rolling back clean energy targets — the more recent and more definitive evidence.

Rabon was listed as a sponsor of sports betting legalization. Bill passed Senate but failed House by 1 vote (51-50) in 2022. Sports betting was later legalized in 2023. Limited relevance to civic axes.
Rabon was instrumental in removing Sunday hunting restrictions in NC. Consistent with pro-gun-rights, pro-outdoor-sports constituency.

keyVotes.bill: SR 370 — Opposition to Federal Catch Shares for Coastal Fisheries (2017)
keyVotes.notes: Rabon sponsored Senate Resolution opposing federal fisheries management restrictions. Consistent with anti-federal-regulatory stance.

Rabon was credited with being willing to work with Democrats on police reform as Rules Chair, since all legislation passes through his committee. The bill made bipartisan changes to law enforcement oversight. However, the ACLU of NC criticized it for barring public access to critical information, undermining accountability. Rabon's facilitation of the bill is not equivalent to endorsing strong oversight; it was a compromise measure.

keyVotes.bill: NC Senate 2025 Budget (tax cuts, DOGE-style review)
keyVotes.notes: NC Senate passed $32.6B budget with personal income tax cut to 2.49% by 2030 (additional triggers to 1.99%), a DOGE-style review of state agencies, $700M Helene relief, and small employee raises. Rabon as Rules Chair set the procedural pace and was cited by critics as enabling a 'rushed, untransparent process.' Budget sides with wealthy over social spending (NC Budget & Tax Center analysis).

positionConflicts.conflict: In 2021, Rabon voted for or allowed passage of HB951 setting NC's 70% carbon reduction by 2030 goal. In 2025, he co-sponsored SB266 to eliminate that same 2030 interim target. His 2025 action is the more definitive signal — he appears to have supported the compromise in 2021 but then used his majority-control to roll it back when the coalition shifted.
sources: SB266 (2025) NC General Assembly — Rabon listed as co-sponsor

positionConflicts.conflict: Rabon is listed as supporting HB76 Medicaid expansion (2023), which expanded coverage to ~600K low-income NC residents. However, he frames healthcare positions consistently as market-based reform (CON law repeal, drug transparency, nursing scope of practice) rather than coverage expansion. The Senate version of HB76 was conditioned on CON reform and was supported by Senate Republican leaders as a trade, not a shift toward government coverage. His overall healthcare scorecard is market-oriented.

Rabon's B+ NORML rating for medical marijuana advocacy stands in contrast to his otherwise very conservative public-health record (anti-vaccine mandate, anti-collective-mandate positions inferred from party record). His marijuana position is grounded in personal medical experience and libertarian framing, not progressive public health philosophy.

safety_net_breadth.evidence: Consistent voting for budgets that reduce social spending relative to tax cuts for upper-income earners. NC Budget & Tax Center analysis shows 2023-2025 budget priorities wealth-concentrated tax cuts over safety net. Senate caucus leadership on budgets that trim state agency spending ('DOGE-style review' 2025). Supported Medicaid expansion only in conditioned form (work requirements allowed, CON reform trade).

public_investment.evidence: 99.3 NCFREE score (near-perfect free-enterprise rating). Sponsored SB651 to cut income tax below 2.5%. Consistently voted for multi-year income tax reduction glide paths. As Rules Chair, shaped budgets that deepen tax cuts at the expense of public programs. Exception: supported large Hurricane Helene recovery appropriations ($700M+), which may reflect disaster response rather than general public investment philosophy.

school_choice.evidence: Voted (as Senate Rules Chairman, party-line Republican) for HB10 and related bills expanding Opportunity Scholarship program from ~$113M to $463.5M additional funding, with escalation to $825M/year by 2032-33. Voted to override Governor's veto. All voucher expansion votes were party-line Republican, and Rabon is the most senior Senate Republican after Berger.

coverage_model.evidence: Supported market-side healthcare reforms: CON law reform, drug price transparency (SB479, SB316, SB315, SB537), nurse scope of practice expansion — all framed as reducing government regulation, not expanding government coverage. Supported Medicaid expansion HB76 (2023) as a conditional trade with CON reform. This is not single-payer or public-option support. Near-perfect NCFREE score reinforces market orientation.

cost_control.evidence: Supported drug transparency bills, CON law reform, and nursing scope-of-practice bills — all market-competition/deregulation mechanisms for cost control. No evidence of supporting government price controls or rate-setting. AffordableCareNC positions (SB479, SB316, SB315, SB537) all use market mechanisms.

public_health.evidence: Medical marijuana advocacy is individual-rights-based, not collective mandate. Party-line Republican voting record overall. No evidence of supporting COVID mandates, vaccine requirements, or other collective public health mandates. His healthcare framing is consistently patient-choice and market-based.

zoning_supply.inferredPosition: Loosen Zoning / More Supply via property-rights lens (toward poleA, but motivated by deregulation not affordability)
zoning_supply.evidence: SB382 (2024) banned local downzoning without all affected property owners' consent — this expands what landowners can do with property (anti-zoning-restriction) but is motivated by property rights and development deregulation, not affordable housing goals. NC Home Builders Association praised it as 'a huge victory for property rights.' Local governments in Rabon's district opposed it. Rabon facilitated SB382's passage through Rules Committee.

affordability_tools.evidence: No direct evidence of supporting government housing subsidies. General free-enterprise/anti-regulation stance suggests opposition to rent control or direct subsidy programs. SB382's framing as property rights expansion, not affordability, is consistent with poleB. Low confidence — limited direct evidence on this axis.

transit_priority.evidence: Rabon serves as Chair of Appropriations on Department of Transportation. District is rural/coastal (Brunswick, Columbus counties) where car dependency is baseline. NC Senate Republican priorities consistently favor road/highway investment over transit. Helene recovery budget includes $560M to rebuild roads and bridges. No evidence of transit advocacy. Low confidence — no direct transit votes found.

police_accountability.inferredPosition: Moderate — facilitated bipartisan reform but within constrained parameters (toward poleB)
police_accountability.evidence: As Rules Chair, Rabon was credited with working with Democrats to pass NC's 2021 police reform bill. However, ACLU-NC criticized the bill for barring public access to critical accountability information. The measure was a procedural compromise, not a strong accountability bill. Rabon's individual position on police oversight is not clearly documented. Low confidence.
police_accountability.notes: Insufficient evidence to score this axis with confidence. The 2021 bill was a bipartisan procedural vehicle; Rabon's personal position is unclear.

sentencing_goals.evidence: Republican Senate caucus leader; 2023 fiscal notes reference legislation creating new misdemeanor/felony classes and sentencing enhancements. General Republican positioning. No specific sentencing reform advocacy found. Low confidence.
sentencing_goals.notes: Insufficient direct evidence to score with confidence.

firearms_policy.evidence: Voted YES on SB50 (permitless carry) both on passage and veto override (2025). Primary sponsor of Sunday hunting expansion (2017). Avid hunter and fisherman. Sponsored SR370 opposing federal fisheries management restrictions. District is rural/coastal with strong gun culture. Voting record consistent with A-range NRA alignment. No evidence of supporting any gun regulations.

ambition_level.evidence: Co-sponsored SB266 (2025) eliminating NC's 2030 70%-carbon-reduction interim target from HB951 — the most significant rollback of clean energy policy in NC in years. Voted for veto override. NC Chamber supported it; NRDC, Sierra Club, NC Justice Center, and Governor Stein opposed it. His 2013 procedural blocking of the renewable energy standard repeal (a nuanced older signal) is superseded by this direct co-sponsorship of a rollback.

energy_portfolio.evidence: SB266 allows cost-recovery for new carbon-emitting generation resources — explicitly opening the door to continued fossil fuel investment. The NC Sustainable Energy Association and SEIA criticized SB266 as a 'step back' for NC's clean energy economy. Rabon's NCFREE score and free-enterprise orientation aligns with fossil-fuel-permissive energy policy.

permitting_speed.inferredPosition: Standard Review Process / No urgency for green permitting (toward poleB)
permitting_speed.evidence: No direct evidence on permitting speed specifically. His general anti-regulatory, pro-market stance and SB266 support suggest he would oppose expedited permitting for renewables at the expense of standard review. Low confidence — no direct bill votes found.

notableNuances: Medical marijuana advocacy (B+ NORML) is genuine and personal but conservatively framed — individual access, not public health reform.
Medicaid expansion support (HB76 2023) was conditional on market deregulation (CON reform) and is not evidence of single-payer or public-option sympathies.
SB382 downzoning ban expands what developers can build but is property-rights motivated, not affordability-motivated.
Rabon's most powerful influence is procedural (Rules Chair) — he shapes the legislative calendar more than any individual floor vote suggests.
Long pattern of media disengagement means few direct quotes on policy positions — voting record and sponsored bills are primary evidence.
evidenceSummary.keyConflict: Climate record shows tension: supported HB951 (2021 bipartisan clean energy bill) then co-sponsored SB266 (2025) to roll back its interim targets. The 2025 action is the current, controlling signal.
